history: always-repro'd v1.6.2112..v1.9.2607 and main-debug (89e2f98e2); v1.8.2405's clean bisect result is a confirmed invalid-probe artifact (unrelated global-namespace collision with the builtin 'integral_constant' added by PR #6156, itself fixed by PR #6700 before v1.8.2407 -- see notes.md), not a fix. v1.4.1907..v1.6.2106 are invalid-probes (HV 2021 did not exist yet). v1.6.2112 (2021-12-08) predates the 2023-08-05 filing by ~20 months, so the checkable history covers the issue's whole life.
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: A scoped enum's enumerator is rejected as a non-type template argument even when the template parameter's declared type is that exact enum type (repro.hlsl: 'non-type template argument of type ENUM is not an integral constant expression'); the identical pattern with a plain enum compiles, and gcc accepts the scoped-enum version, so this is a DXC-specific gap. The original report's array-index half is not a bug -- gcc rejects the same uncast scoped-enum array index identically. Duplicate #6706 already carries a maintainer statement that DXC will not get further investment here and that Clang does not have the gap; the hlsl_clang_trunk godbolt pane now confirms that directly.
title: C++11 enums don’t work as integer constants as expected
